text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 4.2% today after oil prices tumbled below $100 a barrel on signs that diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran might ease Middle East tensions. The stock had climbed steadily through mid-week as geopolitical fears drove oil higher, but that momentum reversed when Trump signaled openness to negotiating with Iran, reducing the supply-shock premium that had pushed crude from the mid-$90s to the $420s on the stock price.

Refiners like Marathon profit when they can buy crude cheaply and sell refined products at a wider margin, so a $30 drop in oil prices in a single day cuts into those spreads significantly. Even though U.S. refineries are running near full capacity at 96.8% and storage levels remain relatively tight, the market's sudden shift from "geopolitical crisis" to "possible deal" erased the fear premium that had been supporting energy stocks all week.
